evidence.issue:
A problem with setting AxiosError.prototype.toJSON
### Describe the bug

`util.inherits` fails on `Object.assign(props)` when `Error.prototype.toJSON`  is already defined as a non-writable. 

We're using a library that adds a toJSON to the prototype of Error.
It does it using something in the spirit of:
```
Object.defineProperty(Error.prorotype, 'toJSON', { configurable: true, writable: false, enumerable: false, value() {
  /* some customization code  that makes sure name, stack and any own property passes */ 
})
```
Then, `axios/lib/util.js:inerit` fails on `Object.assign`.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d4147783-fe1c-4ed4-a2eb-bd4919cae0a8)

Also - see reproduction below.


### To Reproduce

Case isolated in the code snippet below.

### Code snippet

```js
Object.defineProperty(Error.prototype, 'toJSON', {
  configurable: true,
  writable: false,
  enumerable: false,
  value: function foo() { return {} }
})

const utils = (await import(path.join(process.cwd(), 'node_modules/axios/lib/utils.js'))).default

function MyError() { }

//This does not work (throws):
utils.inherits(MyError, Error, { toJSON() { return {} } }) //<-- throws: TypeError: Cannot assign to read only property 'toJSON' of object 'Error'

//This does not throw, and works as expected:
const util = require('node:util')
util.inherits(MyError, Error, { toJSON() { return {} } })
```


### Expected behavior

- Should not throw
- Should set the toJSON on the extended prototype

### Axios Version

1.7.7

evidence.comment:C1:
This issue does not seem to be a bug; rather, it is expected behavior.

For property inheritance, Axios's `utils.inherits()` assigns properties to the child's `constructor.prototype` using the `Object.assign()` method.

Because `Object.assign()` *assigns* properties, it could throw a TypeError if a property is non-writable, as explained in the [MDN Web Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Object/assign#description). According to your code snippet, you defined `toJSON` as non-writable property, so it's natural for it to throw.

However, Node's `util.inherits()` does not provide functionality that inherits properties by assigning them. It only accepts two parameters: the child and the super constructor.

So on your working example `util.inherits(MyError, Error, { toJSON() { return {} } })`, the third parameter will just be ignored because functions in JavaScript do not throw errors for extra arguments.

Here's the actual code definition in node: [util.js:321](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v20.18.0/lib/util.js#L321)

And here's the code in axios: [utils.js:360](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/main/lib/utils.js#L360)
